t: You're looking at the Frieze of Parnassus, a large sculpted stone frieze that runs all the way round the base of the Albert Memorial. The memorial was built in the 1860s in memory of Prince Albert, Queen Victoria's husband. Two sculptors made the frieze. Henry Hugh Armstead was a sculptor and illustrator influenced by the Pre-Raphaelites. John Birnie Philip was a nineteenth-century sculptor who did much of his work for the architect Sir George Gilbert Scott. Take a slow walk around the podium and you can follow the frieze as it goes.
